title: Repairing a Wobbly Chair
content:
A wobbly chair feels small, but it changes how you use a room. The fix is usually simple: reattach a loose joint and give it time to set.

Most chairs wobble because the glue in one joint has weakened. You do not need fancy tools, just patience and a steady clamp.

Check the joints

Rock the chair gently and watch which leg moves first. That is the joint you will start with.

Gather a basic kit

  • Wood glue or carpenters glue.
  • Two clamps, or a strap clamp for tricky frames.
  • A thin putty knife or old credit card.
  • A damp cloth for cleanup.

Open the joint and clean it

If the joint is loose, ease it apart just enough to get glue inside. Use the putty knife to scrape out old, flaky glue so the new glue can bond.

Glue and clamp

Brush a thin layer of glue on both surfaces, press the joint together, and clamp it snugly. Wipe away squeeze out with a damp cloth.

Let it cure

Leave the chair clamped for at least six hours, then wait a full day before sitting on it. The bond keeps strengthening as it cures.

Prevent future wobble

  • Lift the chair instead of dragging it.
  • Keep it away from direct heat that dries out wood.
  • Check and tighten joints once a year.
Small repairs are the fastest way to make a space feel cared for.

Once the chair is steady again, you will notice the room feels quieter. Solid furniture lets you focus on the moment instead of the wobble.
